question: ap1
prompt:
Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

It is 2036. Looking back, 5 landmark papers each settled this question in a way that surprised the field, because of how they approached it. For each paper, describe what it measured, analyzed, or did, as a concrete idea a research lab could pursue today. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Paper 1 (hypothetical): Degron washout of AP-1 after priming
ideas.description: Use an auxin- or dTAG-inducible degron to remove Fos or Jun after a priming stimulus, then measure chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq) and the transcriptional response to re-stimulation at days to weeks. If the primed state survives AP-1 loss, AP-1 is needed to establish memory but not to maintain it; if it collapses, AP-1 is the maintenance mechanism.

ideas.title: Paper 2 (hypothetical): Tracking AP-1 through mitosis
ideas.description: Tag endogenous Jun or Fos with HaloTag or a similar label for live imaging across cell divisions, and run CUT&Tag on sorted mitotic cells to see whether AP-1 stays bound to memory enhancers during mitosis. Then test whether daughter cells inherit accessibility and the primed response. Mitotic retention would support bookmarking as a memory mechanism.

ideas.title: Paper 3 (hypothetical): Optogenetic pulse-pattern encoding of AP-1
ideas.description: Build light-controlled Fos/Jun constructs and deliver the same total AP-1 dose as pulses of different frequency, duration, or spacing. Compare the resulting memory after a long rest, measured by how strongly cells respond on re-stimulation. This tests whether memory depends on dose, timing, or pattern, which is central to whether AP-1 encodes history.

ideas.title: Paper 4 (hypothetical): Activity-dependent tagging and manipulation of AP-1 engram cells
ideas.description: Use an activity-dependent system (such as a TRAP-style tamoxifen-inducible Fos reporter) to permanently label AP-1-active cells during a learning or immune-challenge event in vivo. Then reactivate or ablate those labeled cells later to test whether they are both necessary and sufficient for the memory-driven response. This moves the question from correlation to causation in a living animal.

ideas.title: Paper 5 (hypothetical): Lineage-barcoded multiomics of trained immunity
ideas.description: Introduce a DNA barcode into hematopoietic progenitors, prime them in vivo with a single AP-1-driving stimulus, and then run single-cell multiome (RNA plus ATAC) on barcoded clonal descendants months later. Comparing primed and unprimed clones shows whether AP-1-dependent memory is carried by specific progenitor lineages, and whether it is heritable across the clone.
